data.name: Moselle
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Moselle was a river goddess. Her name means 'Water megas (great)'. She was often depicted as a beautiful nymph who protected the rivers and ensured their bountiful flow. In Christianity, the name Moselle may symbolize the living water of eternal life.

in_hebrew.name: מוסלאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From Hebrew 'moshel' (מושל) meaning 'to save, deliver, protect, or rescue'. The name Moselle is derived from this root and means 'God is my savior' or 'God saves'.

in_greek.name: Μοσελλη
in_greek.long_meaning: From Greek 'moselle' (Μοσελλη), derived from 'mosis' (μοσις) meaning 'saving, deliverance, or salvation'. The name Moselle in Greek means 'saved by God'.

in_latin.name: Mosella
in_latin.long_meaning: From Latin 'mosella' (Mosella), derived from 'mos' (mos) meaning 'saving, deliverance, or salvation', and 'ella' (ella) meaning 'God'. The name Moselle in Latin means 'God's savior'.

in_english.name: Moselle
in_english.long_meaning: From Old French 'mosel' or 'moselle', derived from the Latin 'mosella', meaning 'God's savior'. Alternatively, it could be derived from the Old French 'mosel' meaning 'mossy, covered with moss'. The name Moselle in English can mean 'savior' or 'God's savior'.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Moselle" has its origins in Greek mythology, where Moselle was a river goddess. The name "Moselle" means 'Water megas (great)' and was often depicted as a beautiful nymph who protected the rivers and ensured their bountiful flow. This name has been passed down through history and has been used as a name for places, particularly in Europe, such as the Moselle River in France and Germany.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Moselle may symbolize the living water of eternal life, as referenced in the Bible where Jesus said "let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink. Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within them" (John 7:37-38). The name may also evoke images of spiritual sustenance and refreshment, offering a sense of renewal and hope. Additionally, Moselle may represent a connection to the divine through the natural world and the power of water as a symbol of life and renewal.
